validity.researcher_notes: The gem.wiki page's ONLY reference (cite_note-1) is 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75' -> https://www.opec.org/opec_web/static_files_project/media/downloads/publications/ASB2012.pdf. Ran url_verifier with expected token 'Waha': FAIL — 200 but missing expected. Manually fetched the URL directly (urllib + curl, distinct UAs): it now resolves to the generic OPEC.org homepage/nav shell (title 'Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries', full of menu text like 'About Us / Member Countries / Libya / Nigeria...'), NOT the actual 2012 Annual Statistical Bulletin PDF — the file path is dead/moved (soft-404, HTTP 200 but wrong content, Content-Type text/html). Even setting the dead-link problem aside, the OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin is a country-level aggregate reserves/production/trade tables publication — it has never itemized named internal Libyan gas-gathering pipeline segments like 'Waha-Nasser', so it would not have supported this specific claim even when live. Checked wiki_citations.json for the other 29 in-scope rows: this EXACT same ASB2012.pdf URL is reused verbatim as the sole citation on at least 10 sibling pages (P1859, P1861, P1866, P1867, P1868, P1869, P1870, P1871, P1872, and P1860 itself) — confirming it is a boilerplate/generic citation pasted across a whole cluster of Sirte Basin internal segment pipelines, not evidence specific to any one of them. Open-web search (English and Arabic) for 'Waha-Nasser gas pipeline' returns only gem.wiki itself and its mirrors/aggregators; nothing independent names a pipeline called 'Waha-Nasser'. Independently confirmed both endpoints are real, distinct entities: Waha field is operated by Waha Oil Co (NOC/ConocoPhillips/TotalEnergies/Hess JV), while Nasser field (formerly Zelten, Libya's first major oil field, discovered 1959) is ~169 km south of Brega and is operated by Sirte Oil Co, a DIFFERENT NOC subsidiary (offshore-technology.com field profile, Wikipedia Zelten oil field, globalsecurity.org Libya petrol background) -- i.e. current Operator/Owner values (Waha Oil Co / NOC+ConocoPhillips+TotalEnergies+Hess) describe the Waha-side JV only and may not be the right attribution if this pipeline genuinely runs to Nasser field's Sirte-Oil-operated infrastructure. One WebSearch AI-summary claimed globalsecurity.org lists 'Defa-Nasser; Nasser-Hatiba; Nasser(Zelten)-Marsa el Brega; Waha-Es Sider' as Libya's major pipelines (notably NOT 'Waha-Nasser') — but I fetched that page directly and this pipeline list does NOT appear anywhere in the actual HTML; the search tool's synthesis appears to have fabricated/merged it from elsewhere, so I am explicitly NOT relying on or citing it. Net: no independent source of any kind could be found that names a 'Waha-Nasser' gas pipeline, the row's own cited source is both dead and generically non-specific (and is reused wholesale across ~10 other rows), and there is a plausible mechanism for how it could be a conflation (two real, separately-operated Sirte Basin fields/nodes stitched into a pipeline name GEM invented for a network diagram). Recommend treating as an unconfirmed/possible-hallucination entity pending a real primary source (Waha Oil Co / NOC technical document, EIA/USGS Sirte Basin infrastructure map, or a news report) rather than accepting the current spec values (177 km / 24 in / 5.66 bcm/y / operating) at face value. Did not add any refs — nothing passed verification.

summary: Existence concern: sole wiki citation (OPEC ASB2012.pdf) is dead (resolves to opec.org homepage, not the PDF) and is boilerplate reused verbatim across 10+ sibling Sirte-Basin segment pipelines; no independent source anywhere names a 'Waha-Nasser' gas pipeline, though both endpoint fields (Waha, operated by Waha Oil Co; Nasser/Zelten, operated by a different NOC subsidiary Sirte Oil Co) are independently real.
